thread.title: Netflix downgraded at KeyBanc due to pace of spending and length of time for a return

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Netflix downgraded at KeyBanc due to pace of spending and length of time for a return
text:
Netflix is spending at an elevated clip and the returns on its investments may not materialize soon.
That is the view of KeyBanc analysts, who downgraded the streaming-video provider to sector weight from overweight on the heels of blowout results that sent shares NFLX, +3.98% soaring 11% late Tuesday in premarket trade.
Netflix has no problem in growing its subscriber base, but “substantial upside” for shares from here will require further revenue growth and accelerating profits, which hasn’t gone as fast as the entertainment giant hoped, said Andy Hargreaves and a team at KeyBanc, in a note to clients.
See Also Why a Brexit Deal Between the U.K. and the EU Remains Elusive × “While we maintain a favorable view of Netflix’s strategic positioning, we believe improving investment efficiency or significant ancillary opportunities are needed to drive upside from current levels, and we don’t anticipate either over the next year,” said a team of KeyBanc analysts led by Andy Hargreaves.
Netflix added a net 6.96 million subscribers in the third quarter, blowing past expectations, after a second-quarter miss on those numbers, which sent shares careening lower in July . The Los Gatos, Calif., company sees more subscribers hopping on board in the fourth quarter. But it also plans on maintaining its spending rate, estimates KeyBanc’s analysts, who forecast free cash flow of around negative $3 billion for 2018.
Read: Netflix is ditching freeloaders from subscriber forecasts after volatile stock moves
“We believe Netflix’s leadership position in subscription video provides long-term opportunities to build revenue in consumer products, advertising, broad theatrical releases, and mobile-only subscriptions,” said Hargreaves and the team. But those opportunities could take “several years to develop” and are at risk from rising interest rates and growing competition over the next year.
Netflix shares have shot up 80% this year so far, making it the fourth-best performing stock among constituents of the S&P 500 SPX, +2.15% The company, run by Reed Hastings, also has outperformed a clutch of highflying technology and internet-related stocks known as FAANG—Facebook Inc. FB, +3.43% Apple Inc. AAPL, +2.20% Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +3.35% and Alphabet’s Google Inc. GOOGL, +2.78%
Raymond James and Goldman Sachs recently cut their price targets , citing investor jitters over rising interest rates and trade tensions. However, they were upbeat on Netflix’s long-term prospects, while Citigroup lifted Netflix to buy from neutral last Friday, saying last week’s two-day market rout was a chance to pick up the stock.
Even after the summer results that sent shares tumbling, Wall Street analysts largely stood by the Hastings’s streaming-video provider, including KeyBanc, though they lowered their share price target to $375.
“Given our positive ongoing view of the business, a lower stock price or evidence of improving investment efficiency would likely prompt us to resume a more-positive view of the shares,” said the analysts.
